sections.text: मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो।
If Thou thinkest that it can be made possible for me to see it, show me, O Lord of Lords, Thine own Eternal Self.
Lord Shri Krishna replied: Behold, O Arjuna! My celestial forms, by hundreds and thousands, various in kind, in colour and in shape.

Behold thou the Powers of Nature: fire, earth, wind and sky; the sun, the heavens, the moon, the stars; all forces of vitality and of healing; and the roving winds. See the myriad wonders revealed to none but thee.

We had been discussing Chapter 11, the Vishwarupadarshan, the cosmic form of the Lord. In the beginning of chapter 11, Arjuna said: Anugrahaya, out of your compassion for me, you gave me this deepest secret about the self and showed me how to experience that and meditate on it. However, thats not sufficient for me to understand the nature of the self which you have described.
He said, my delusion is dispelled -- the delusion about myself. When he started in the first chapter saying, I cannot kill these people even if I get killed, Bhagavan said in the second chapter that the self cannot be killed. The self in you is imperishable, immutable.
The self in you is the same self in everyone else. So one who thinks he is a slayer and one who thinks he is slain -- both are wrong, because it is like within myself: I cannot be both slayer and slain of my own self. Arjuna said, now Im very clear.
My confusion about what my self is, that is gone. However, Im still at a level where I cannot comprehend the unity of all beings. I understand.
I can also experience my own self. Im very aware of myself. I can now theoretically understand that as my self is imperishable, your self is also imperishable.
However, that oneness of the self is beyond my understanding. If you really look at this point of the Bhagavad Gita, we are exactly at the same level -- all of us who have been sincerely seeking to understand the nature of the self. All this is intellectually understood.
But when it comes to realizing, myself and yourself is one and the same understanding falls apart from experience. My experience is very different in day to day life. I know everything about myself and how I feel, but I cannot relate to yourself and how you feel.
Therefore, Arjuna said, I am very clear. You have also explained to me how the things come into being and how they perishes all comes out of the same self and perishes back into the same self. It is very clear to me.
However, this oneness of the Lord, the glory of the supreme Self -- to be perceived as one and not as many -- is beyond my control right now. And thats the hurdle in the path of my realization. Right now Im in a constant samadhi about myself.
This conditioned self which I think is me requires no effort to realize. Its automatic knowledge. As soon as a baby is born, he or she knows this is me and everyone else is someone else.
So thats an automatic knowledge. Were conditioned by that. The conditioned self has conditioned us to think who we are.
The knowledge given to us by the sages telling us that no, this conditioned self is not the only nature of yourself. Yourself is omnipresent, omnipotent and omniscient. Youre just conditioning it and making it limited yourself.
Once you let go of those limitations, you will identify with the Supreme Self. And thats where Arjuna says, I have a difficulty. I cant experience that.
I want to experience that form of the self -- your form. You claim to know that supreme form of the self. I know this limited form of the self; you know the supreme form.
I need to see that to get over the hurdle. So he said, drastumi chami te rupam aishwaram purushottamam. O Lord of all the beings.
Purushottam, I want to say that form of yours where everything is included in one. I see myself as separate. The world is separate.
The world of plurality is very easy for me to comprehend. But I want to see all in its totality. That if you think that it is possible for me to see.
So Bhagavan said, okay, I think you are ready for it. You come to that level of understanding that the only barrier left is your own intellect. The only barrier left is your own conditioning.
You have accepted fully that my self and the selves of others are one and the same. By inference, we have come to the conclusion that we cannot be anything but part of the same self. If the Lord created this universe out of his Self -- no other material was available to him, and both the universe and the Lord exist -- then the material for this universe is the Lords Self.
If my self is created out of the Lords Self, then my self and his self cannot be different. So is the case for everything else which I see. However, that oneness which I should feel -- which I am feeling in my own body, in my own limited self -- I have complete oneness there.
There is never an argument about the left hand versus the right hand, no argument about the right eye versus the left eye. If one is weak, the other takes over. You dont even realize when that happens, because theres a complete oneness in it.
But thats not happening with my family members or my community members. If someone is suffering, to some extent I will help, but not to the extent that I would help myself. Arjuna said, let me see that oneness with all beings.
In Verse 5, Sri Bhagavan Vacha Pashame Partharu Pani Satasa Athah Sahastra Saha Nana Vidhani Divyani Nana Varana Krutinicha. Krishna says: I will let you see my form which has hundreds and thousands of forms in it, various types of divine shapes and colors. In my own being you will see hundreds and thousands of forms -- the forms which you have seen till now and forms which you have not seen -- in a flash, all at once.
So you will see hundreds and thousands of forms, various colors, various types, and various shapes. And in the next verse he says Pashya, Aditya, Rudra, Asvinau, Marutahata, Bahuni, Adristha, Purvani, Pasha, Acharyani, Bharada. He said, not only will you see the forms you are familiar with, but you will also see forms you are not familiar with.
Not only the forms and beings which you want to see in one, but also the divine beings which you have been worshipping as someone other than this world. All these deities they were worshiping in Vedic times -- Aditya (Surya), Rudra (basically Shiva, the aspect of destruction in the Trinity), Vasu, all these various deities of nature, Maruta the wind God -- all the gods which you have been worshipping, you will see them also in the same being. Currently your understanding is that this is Mrityu Lok.
We are the mortal beings, and the divine beings are separate. So we worship the divine beings as mortals. And they seem to be completely different from myself and the selves of the people in the mortal world.
But Bhagavan says, when you see them -- those divine beings -- all will be part of the one self, my own self, your own self. And you will see all that. Then Bahuni Adrishta Purvani -- even things you never imagined or thought about before, Sacchara and Achara, the moving and unmoving beings, you will see as one self.
Yacha Anya Drastum Ichasi -- he says, here in this one location, everything is complete without leaving anything out. The whole universe centered in one being, including all the moving and unmoving. As I said, you will see all these things, plus whatever else you desire to see.
Because, you see, we always have a conception of divinity. A Hindu will say, when Bhagavan appears, in what form will he come? Either Rama or Krishna or Shiva -- and that too in the same form as we have been seeing in calendars and pictures. If he comes in a different form, we dont accept him as Bhagavan.
He has to have the mukut and all those things. So, whatever you want to see, you will see in myself. However, the technical difficulty is that you wont be able to see it with your natural eyes.
Natu maam shakya seydrastum anay neva swachakshusa Divyam dadami teksuhu pashame yogameshwaram. No matter how much we are taught to look at the world differently, unless we change our way of seeing things, well always go back to seeing what we were seeing before. To learn new things and to look at this world in a different way, we have to change our perception.
So Divyam dadami tejaksho -- Im giving you this divine vision, meaning Im going to change your way of seeing things. The way of my seeing things right now may be well, I am this and you are that. After about two generations we call ourselves, we are Indians and they are Americans.
Somebody says, are you not American also? Youre an American citizen. You had been living here for like 30 years. No, no, Im an Indian or Im an American, but Im Indian.
Till I change my perception of seeing myself as part of this country, as an American, I will never be able to see myself as part of it. Nothing changes, but my perception about seeing things changes. That perception change is very much required.
Go outside right now. The way you see this world, no matter how much I tell you to see it as one -- we can say the space is in the room, or the room is in the space. I can continue seeing this space in the room until I start visualizing that the space is everywhere, including in this room.
And that visualization has to change. The perception has to change to see what Arjuna wanted to see. So now, what is it that stands between my perception and the unity of myself and yourself? There are two things.
One is, I am separated from you by the space between us. This conditioned self and that conditioned self have a space between them. So as soon as we have this perception of space, we create this world of plurality.
This space, just like anything that we can imagine, is an imaginary thing. Is there space in existence? When you put two things, a space is created between two things. If you remove both, there is no space.
Space can only be seen in relationship to the objects we perceive. How much space is between you and me can only be defined by first defining where you and I are. If you remove you and I, there is no space to be measured.
So this space is a conception of my mind. Once I conceived of myself as an entity separate from you as an entity, the space was created. And then the second thing which separates myself and others is time.
I met such and such person yesterday, but hes not here today. So Im separated from him by time. My father lived in a different time.
Im living in a different time. Im separated by time. From Einstein onward, we know time is nothing but a concept of our mind.
Time depends on the position of the observer. When we say we are seeing the same thing at the same time, it depends on where you and I are. We see the stars at night and say, That star is doing this right now. But we know the light takes many, many years to come here.
So what we see today actually existed many years ago, but we consider it now. We consider that in the past. We consider what well see tomorrow is in future. Now all this thing is dependent on my station point in life.
My time is defined by my conditioning.

In these verses, Krishna promises to show Arjuna forms by hundreds and thousands, various in kind, in colour and in shape - including the Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Ashvins, and Maruts. But crucially, Krishna warns that Arjuna cannot see this with his ordinary eyes - a divine vision (divya chakshus) must be granted. This points to a fundamental limitation we all face: our programmed way of seeing the world keeps us trapped in duality. We are conditioned from birth to see I as separate from the world, and this conditioning acts like a filter that obscures unity.
Consider how your perception creates your reality. The same situation can be seen as a threat by one person and an opportunity by another - nothing changes except the way of seeing. Krishna is essentially telling Arjuna: I will change your paradigm, not the world itself. What paradigms or mental filters are you currently looking through? How might your relationships, work, and daily experiences transform if you could truly see through a lens of interconnection rather than separation?
Today, practice shifting your perspective intentionally. When you see individual objects - trees, cars, people - try to also perceive the space that contains them all. When you notice differences between yourself and others, simultaneously recognize what you share: consciousness, the desire for happiness, the experience of being alive. This practice of holding both perspectives - the many and the One - is the beginning of developing that divine sight Krishna speaks of.
